title: Two Roads to Durable Agents: Replay vs. Snapshot — Eric Allam, CEO, Trigger.dev
talk_summary: Eric Allam argues durable agents need two separate durability mechanisms: an append-only context log (all LLM/tool messages) for cross-version and cross-failure recovery, and execution-state snapshots (Firecracker microVMs with seekable compression) to pause/resume the machine cheaply between turns. He contrasts this with the older 'replay' workflow model, whose journal grows unboundedly and becomes rigid for long-lived agent sessions.

takeaways.technique: Separate context log from execution state
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the agent's message/tool-call history as an append-only log stored in a DB/object store, independent of the compute that produced it, so a run can resume on a new code version or after a crash.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the context is first and the most important, and it's just an append-only log of sort of everything that happened

takeaways.technique: Snapshot/restore instead of keeping VMs live
takeaways.what_they_do: Snapshot the whole microVM when an agent is idle waiting for input, shut it down, and restore on the next message, instead of paying to keep the machine running.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of recreating the execution state from a log, we should use snapshot and restore
takeaways.numbers: snapshots slightly under a second, restores a couple hundred milliseconds; ~14MB compressed snapshot vs 512MB default

takeaways.what_they_do: Compress snapshots with seekable compression and decompress only the memory pages needed at restore time, plus layering, to shrink snapshot size and restore latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually don't restore all the memory pages at once ... just like decompress like that little bit that needs to be

takeaways.technique: Avoid unbounded replay journals for long sessions
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that wrapping every LLM/tool call as a replay step makes the journal grow until it hits entry-count or entry-size limits, and replay journal versioning breaks on redeploy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as you sort of keep interacting with the agent, the log grows and grows and grows. At a certain point, you might hit into some sort of like fundamental limit

takeaways.technique: Recovery strategy depends on failure type
takeaways.what_they_do: On LLM/rate-limit failures, snapshot and restore when retry is possible; on machine/code failures, recover from the context log.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if there's something wrong with the machine ... You have the context log, and you can recover that
